what_its_for: Asenapine is used to treat schizophrenia (a condition that affects how you think and feel) and bipolar disorder (also called manic-depressive illness, which causes extreme mood swings including highs called mania and lows called depression). It helps balance certain chemicals in your brain to improve your mood, thinking, and behavior.
how_to_take: Asenapine comes as a tablet that dissolves under your tongue (sublingual tablet) and as a skin patch (transdermal patch). For the dissolving tablet: Place it under your tongue and let it dissolve completely — do not chew, crush, or swallow it whole. Do not eat or drink anything for at least 10 minutes after placing the tablet under your tongue. Make sure your hands are dry before handling the tablet. For the skin patch: Apply it to your upper arm, chest, back, or stomach on clean, dry, and hairless skin. Press firmly for 30 seconds. Wear only one patch at a time, and change it every 24 hours. Rotate the spot where you put it each day.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you. The usual starting dose for the dissolving tablet is 5 mg placed under the tongue twice a day (morning and night). Your doctor may increase your dose over time up to 10 mg twice a day depending on how you respond. For the skin patch, the usual dose is one patch (3.8 mg/day, 5.7 mg/day, or 7.6 mg/day) worn for 24 hours and then replaced. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions — do not change your dose without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. For a missed patch: Apply the new patch as soon as you remember, then change it at your next scheduled time.
storage: Store asenapine tablets at room temperature between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep the tablets in their original packaging and do not remove them until you are ready to use them. Keep away from moisture, heat, and direct light. Store skin patches at room temperature and keep them in their sealed pouches until ready to use. Keep all medications safely out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medication down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about the best way to dispose of it.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking asenapine, as it can make drowsiness and dizziness worse and increase the risk of serious side effects. Avoid driving, operating heavy machinery, or doing anything that requires you to be fully alert until you know how this medication affects you, since it can cause drowsiness. Avoid getting up too quickly from sitting or lying down, as asenapine can cause dizziness or lightheadedness, which may lead to falls. Avoid getting too hot — stay out of extreme heat, do not exercise too hard, and stay hydrated, as asenapine can make it harder for your body to cool down. Avoid eating or drinking for at least 10 minutes after taking the sublingual tablet. Tell your doctor or pharmacist about all other medications you take, including over-the-counter drugs and supplements, because some medications can interact with asenapine.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: uncontrollable movements of your face, tongue, or body (this could be a sign of tardive dyskinesia); very high fever, stiff muscles, confusion, or irregular heartbeat (signs of neuroleptic malignant syndrome, a rare but serious reaction); trouble swallowing or breathing; a fast or irregular heartbeat; signs of high blood sugar such as increased thirst, frequent urination, or blurred vision; feeling faint or passing out; signs of low white blood cell count such as fever or frequent infections; severe skin rash or allergic reaction including swelling of the face, lips, or throat; or thoughts of harming yourself. Also call your doctor if you notice numbness or tingling in your mouth after taking the tablet, or if your skin becomes irritated, red, or blistered where you applied the patch.
when_it_works: You may start to notice some improvement in your sleep, agitation, or anxiety within the first few days of taking asenapine. However, it may take several weeks (usually 2 to 4 weeks or longer) to feel the full benefits, such as improved mood, thinking, and overall symptoms. It is important to keep taking your medication every day even if you feel better. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Older adults: Older people (especially those with dementia-related conditions) may be more sensitive to side effects like dizziness, falls, and confusion. Asenapine is not approved for use in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis and may increase the risk of serious complications or death in this group. Pregnancy: Talk to your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Babies born to mothers who took asenapine in the third trimester may have withdrawal symptoms or muscle problems after birth. Breastfeeding: Asenapine may pass into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Children and teenagers: Asenapine (sublingual tablets) can be used in children 10 years and older for bipolar mania, but only under close medical supervision. The skin patch has not been studied in children. Liver problems: If you have severe liver disease, asenapine sublingual tablets should not be used. Talk to your doctor about your liver health.
